name: Maris Thornwell
personality: Methodical, protective of the archive's integrity, prone to anxiety when routines are disrupted. She is not lying, but she is withholding something she considers irrelevant.
dialogue_style: Precise, measured sentences. Uses library terminology. Occasionally corrects the investigator's phrasing.
appearance: A tall woman in her fifties with silver-streaked black hair and ink-stained fingers. She carries a leather notebook at all times.

public_facts: She was in the East Corridor at approximately ten o'clock, returning a trolley of books.
She noticed the light was still on in the Archivist's study when she passed.
She did not enter the study that evening.
She knows the Hourglass is kept on a pedestal by the north window.
private_facts: She saw Corvin Ashwick in the East Corridor at approximately ten past ten, but she did not think it was suspicious at the time — apprentices sometimes work late.
She knows Corvin's thesis project was in serious trouble. She heard him arguing with the Archivist two days ago.

relationships.suspect_corvin: His supervisor for the library cataloguing project. She thinks well of him, perhaps too much so.
relationships.suspect_faelind: Does not trust Faelind's interest in restricted texts.

portrait_description: A careful, intelligent face, slightly drawn with worry tonight.

name: Corvin Ashwick
personality: Ambitious, articulate, visibly anxious tonight. He is the culprit. He is not confessing, but he is also not a practiced liar — he contradicts himself if pressed carefully.
dialogue_style: Speaks quickly, tends to over-explain. Becomes defensive when his thesis is mentioned.
appearance: A young man of about twenty, dark circles under his eyes, robes slightly dishevelled. There is a faint smell of something medicinal about him.

public_facts: He was in the herbarium working on his thesis until late.
He has been studying temporal displacement phenomena.
His thesis is due at the end of the month.
private_facts: He drugged the Archivist's tea with Dreamroot powder.
He took the Hourglass to attempt to reverse a failed experiment that destroyed a month of his thesis work.
He has hidden the Hourglass in the bell tower, inside the old observation box.
He tore a page from a restricted book about Temporal Artifacts two days ago.
He obtained the Dreamroot from a vial he bought in the village, and he discarded the empty vial in the herbarium waste bin.

relationships.suspect_maris: His library supervisor. He respects her and feels guilty about what he has done.
relationships.suspect_faelind: Friendly acquaintances. He knows Faelind wanted the Hourglass for a different reason.

portrait_description: Bright eyes that won't quite meet yours tonight.

name: Faelind Grewe
personality: Warm, perceptive, genuinely concerned about the Archivist's wellbeing. She has her own reasons for wanting the Hourglass but did not take it.
dialogue_style: Speaks thoughtfully, often pauses to consider. Uses healer's terminology when describing the Archivist's condition.
appearance: A young woman with close-cropped red hair and healer's green robes. She smells of medicinal herbs.

public_facts: She was in the infirmary most of the evening tending to a student with a mild hexing injury.
She went to check on the Archivist around eleven when he missed his nightly rounds — she found him unconscious.
She recognizes the smell of Dreamroot in the Archivist's study.
private_facts: She had planned to ask the Archivist for temporary use of the Hourglass to slow the progression of a particularly difficult hex — she did not steal it.
She suspects Dreamroot was used but has not reported this officially yet, waiting to see how the investigation unfolds.

relationships.suspect_corvin: Knows him socially. Noticed he seemed stressed recently.

portrait_description: A healer's composure masking genuine distress.
